Thanks for the details and the PO — can confirm we can issue two invoices (EUR and GBP) addressed to the respective legal entities. A couple of quick points:

- VAT: we need the VAT numbers you included (thanks). For the German entity (Finovate GmbH) we will apply the EU reverse-charge (0% VAT) on the invoice provided the DE VAT ID validates. For the UK entity we treat UK B2B supplies per our UK tax guidance — in most B2B cases we issue without UK VAT if a GB VAT ID is supplied, but I’ve looped in Marissa from Finance to confirm.

- Wire instructions (initial): please see the attached payment_instructions_v1.pdf for our recommended collection accounts. Short summary below:
  - EUR collection (preferred for SEPA): ING Netherlands N.V.
    - Beneficiary: Redwood Inference BV
    - IBAN: NL91INGB0001234567
    - BIC/SWIFT: INGBNL2A
    - Reference: RED-2028-0118-FINOVATE
  - GBP collection (nostro / domestic GBP): Barclays Bank UK
    - Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd
    - Account: 34567890
    - Sort code: 20-30-40
    - SWIFT: BARCGB22
    - Reference: RED-2028-0118-FINOVATE

Note on intermediary fees / FX: depending on which route your bank takes, intermediary/correspondent banks can debit fees either from the sender or the beneficiary, and sometimes the receiving bank passes those along to the beneficiary. We have two options to reduce unpredictability:
  1) Send payments via the exact currency collection account for the invoice currency (EUR -> EUR IBAN; GBP -> GBP account) to avoid FX conversion and extra correspondent hops.
  2) Use our payments partner (GlobalPay Solutions) to accept the payment in the sender’s local currency and settle to us net — this often removes intermediary fees on the customer side but may include a small FX margin.

Can you confirm you’ll instruct two separate wires (one EUR SEPA to the ING account, one GBP domestic to Barclays)? If you prefer Redwood to absorb intermediary fees for the pilot payment, let us know and I’ll leave final sign-off to Finance (cc’d).
